Next steps: share security pack, run quick embedding throughput benchmark, and follow up with pricing and pilot plan.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Head of ML - Aegis), Maya Chen (Director of Search - Aegis), Evan Brooks (SRE - Aegis)

Auto Summary: (auto-gen, may be rough) - Aegis evaluating embedding + reranking flow, currently running hybrid ES + vector DB, exploring Redwood hosted vs dedicated for latency/cost, security controls required for financial data.

Topics: integration with vector DBs, embedding dimensionality, throughput (qps) for re-rank, latency SLOs, hybrid retrieval, SSO / SOC2 / KMS, pilot scope.

Action items (captured): Jordan to send security docs; Priya to propose benchmark test plan; Aegis to share sample query set and expected qps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, joining me is priya our se. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Tom: good, thanks, um, excited to dig in. we only got a 45 minute block so i'll try to be crisp.
[00:10] Maya: hi all, maya here, we'll mostly focus on relevance and throughput questions.
[00:14] Evan: hey, evan, ops and infra, i'll chim in on the deployment and network side.
[00:20] Jordan: great. quick agenda: first, tom give us the context on what you're running today; then priya will walk through how we think about embeddings + rerank on redwood and the hosting options; then q&a and next steps. sound good?
[00:30] Tom: yeah, quick background: we run a customer support search and internal knowledge base, we've been using elasticsearch with BM25 for first-pass, and we spun up a pinecone proof of concept for vector scoring. current pipeline is BM25 top-200 then vector rerank.
[00:46] Tom: qps varies, we're seeing spikes to ~120 qps for search endpoints during peak business hours, average maybe 25 qps. latency SLO is ~200ms P95 for the user-facing latencies, but we can tolerate slightly higher for rerank if first-pass is quick.
[01:05] Maya: re: embeddings, we're currently using 1536-d embeddings from an off-the-shelf model, and have experimented with 1024; curious about tradeoffs for dimensionality with cost and vector DB backends.
[01:18] Jordan: ok, good context. priya, do you want to cover the architecture options and how redwood would plug into that?
[01:22] Priya: sure. so there are a few ways customers do this: for simplest, Redwood Hosted can serve embeddings and generation endpoints — you can keep vectors in your vector DB like Pinecone or Milvus and call Redwood for embed + rerank. for higher throughput and predictable latency, Redwood Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and lower tail latency; and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict data residency/SOC2 requirements.
[01:44] Priya: for the rerank flow specifically we often recommend: 1) BM25 or ANN index first-pass, 2) fetch top-k candidates, 3) call Redwood's rerank endpoint which scores candidate set via cross-encoder or a lightweight bi-encoder + dot-product depending on accuracy/latency tradeoffs.
[02:03] Tom: cross-encoder for rerank is better quality but expensive at scale, right? we've been leaning toward a lightweight bi-encoder with a small cross-encoder sample for re-checking.
[02:13] Priya: exactly — cross-encoder gives the best quality but costs per document since it's pairwise. we can do hybrid: bi-encoder embedding dot-product for the majority and run a cross-encoder on top N for final sort. we support both and have tuning suggestions for batch sizes and sequence truncation.
[02:32] Evan: on integration, how do you recommend storing vectors? we want to keep everything in our control — is it fine to use our own Milvus cluster and just call Redwood for embeddings?
[02:41] Priya: yes, you can host vectors anywhere. typical integration patterns: 1) push embeddings from Redwood to your vector DB (we return the vector from the embed API), 2) store in your DB with metadata, 3) do ANN retrieval in DB, then call rerank. we also have a native option where Redwood can host the index on Dedicated for lower network hop, but that is part of dedicated offering.
[03:03] Tom: what about dimensionality — we saw 1536 is standard for some open models, but 768 is cheaper. what's the impact?
[03:12] Priya: lower dims means smaller memory footprint and faster ANN recalls (and lower network egress and storage costs) but may reduce accuracy. we usually recommend running an A/B on sample query set: evaluate recall/precision vs cost. if you need, Redwood Optimize can give quantization and dimension recommendations per workload.
[03:30] Maya: can you speak to throughput? we need to process ~120 qps peak and during a rerank we might be scoring top 50 per query so that multiplies compute.
[03:40] Priya: yeah concurrency matters. for bi-encoder dot products that's mostly matrix ops and is far cheaper; a cross-encoder at 50 candidates is heavy. on Dedicated you can reserve GPU pools so you get predictable throughput; on Hosted we have autoscaling but peak bursts might hit cold-start variability. for 120 qps with top-50 cross-encoder you'd likely need dedicated or aggressive batching on hosted which can add latency.
[04:07] Tom: ok. what about latency numbers you typically see for rerank on dedicated vs hosted?
[04:14] Priya: ballpark: bi-encoder scoring for top-50 on a mid-sized GPU pool will be sub-50ms per batch depending on sequence length; cross-encoder varies heavily — maybe 5-30ms per pair on optimized runtimes but pairwise multiplies. in practice, customers running cross-encoder heavy workloads pick Dedicated.
[04:33] Evan: network/security — if we use Hosted, what controls do we have around keys and data; we need KMS and audit logs and to prove SOC2 for our security team.
[04:44] Jordan: we can provide SOC2 report and we support customer-managed keys through KMS integrations on Dedicated/Private; Hosted also has encryption at rest and in transit but we can talk about bring-your-own-key for certain plans. i'll send the security pack after this call.
[04:59] Maya: we also have a compliance need to ensure no PII is logged. do you support selective logging or redaction?
[05:05] Priya: yes, we have controls for request/response logging, retention TTLs, and you can opt out of storing request bodies for hosted. Private deployments give full control. we also support audit logs for actions in the console and RBAC.
[05:20] Tom: interesting — one more infra question: can we run nearest-neighbor in our Elastic cluster rather than a separate vector DB?
[05:27] Priya: elastic now has dense vector fields and kNN; it's workable for smaller scale but for large scale high-dim workloads most of our customers pick a dedicated ANN solution like Milvus or Pinecone. the main tradeoff is operator overhead vs performance.
[05:41] Tom: what's involved in a pilot? we want to validate throughput and quality quickly.
[05:46] Jordan: typical pilot is: you share a sample dataset and query set, priya's team helps craft evaluation prompts and we run side-by-side comparison (your current stack vs Redwood pipelines). we can also run a throughput benchmark on dedicated capacity in a short-term trial.
[06:02] Priya: for benchmarks we'll need sample docs, expected qps, and target SLOs. we'll propose a test plan and a script you can run to reproduce.
[06:10] Maya: ok, timeline wise we're aiming for a pilot in 3-4 weeks and procurement hopefully within a quarter depending on results.
[06:18] Tom: pricing — are there clear unit economics we should expect for embedding storage and rerank compute?
[06:23] Jordan: yes we've published pricing for hosted embed and compute; Dedicated is a contract/commit model and we can run some modeled cost estimates based on your qps and candidate sizes. i'll include a cost worksheet in the follow-up.
[06:40] Evan: any pitfalls you've seen customers hit?
[06:44] Priya: common ones: underestimating network egress for frequent embedding calls, running cross-encoder at too high candidate counts, and not caching KV prefix or query-level cache. Redwood has prefix/KV caching and batching features to help reduce cost.
[07:00] Tom: good call. can you also share recommended embedding dims and sample eval metrics we should track?
[07:06] Priya: yes — we'll include recommended dims to test (1536, 1024, 768) and suggested metrics: P@1, MRR, latencies (p50/p95), and cost per query.
[07:18] Jordan: ok we'll recap next steps — i'll send security docs, pricing worksheet, and a pilot proposal. priya will send benchmark plan. you (aegis) will share sample dataset and queries.
[07:29] Maya: sounds good.
[07:31] Tom: thanks, we appreciate it.
[07:33] Evan: thanks everyone.
[07:35] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up by early next week. bye.

(End of recording)
